changelog: Research (done before building, per instruction): Lightweight Charts 4.1.3 (the pinned version) does support the Series Primitives plugin API, but it is a rendering-only mechanism -- dragging, hit-testing and click handling have to be built by hand regardless of which rendering approach is used, so there is no interactivity benefit to attaching to that API's lifecycle. A transparent <canvas> overlay was chosen instead, positioned over the chart and simpler to reason about. More importantly: several reference plugin implementations anchor drawings to Lightweight Charts' own 'logical index' (a bar's position in the currently-loaded array), which was rejected for this app specifically -- js/backtest.js fully replaces its candle array on every single advance/rewind/timeframe-switch, so a logical-index anchor would drift or vanish on the very next step. Every drawing is instead anchored as real {time, price} pairs, converted to pixels fresh via timeToCoordinate()/priceToCoordinate() on every render -- these survive pan, zoom, a timeframe switch, or a completely different loaded window by construction.

New backtest_drawings table (migration, MySQL 8.4-safe) persists drawings per session (a session's own symbol is fixed, so scoping by session_id already scopes by symbol) via a new BacktestDrawingController (get/add/update/delete_backtest_drawing) -- pure CRUD, never read by the replay/order/challenge engine, exactly per the no-lookahead-implications constraint.

Shared behaviour: a vertical toolbar on the left of the chart (cursor, the four tools, magnet toggle, delete); click/drag to place, drag handles or the line body to adjust, Delete to remove the selected drawing, Escape to cancel mid-placement; right-click or double-click opens a settings popover (colour/width/style plus tool-specific options); a magnet option (default on) snaps anchors to the nearest candle's open/high/low/close.

1. Position tool (long and short, separate toolbar buttons): drag to set entry/stop/take-profit, risk zone shaded red and reward zone green, live labels for entry/SL/TP price, R:R ratio, risk in $ and %, and position size (from the session's own risk % and current equity, the same formula backtestPositionSize() already uses server-side). R:R lock, default 3:1: dragging entry or stop keeps the ratio and auto-places TP; dragging TP directly unlocks it and shows the resulting ratio. A Place Order button on the selected tool submits to the existing, unchanged backtest_place_order endpoint using the tool's own levels -- this is what makes 'blocked while the cursor isn't at the latest bar' and 'blocked at the daily trade cap' work for free, both checks already live there. Entry at (within 0.05% of) the current bar's close submits as a market order; anywhere else, a limit order at that entry price. Placing an order deletes the drawing and lets the existing open-positions panel take over as the live marker.

2. Fibonacci retracement: drag between two anchors; default levels 0/0.382/0.5/0.618/0.786/1, no others by default. Settings: per-level enable/colour, extend right, reverse, show price. Price labels render to the right of each level. With magnet on, anchors snap to the nearest candle's wick extremes, same mechanism as every other tool's snapping.
3. Trend line: two-click placement, draggable at either end or as a whole. Settings: colour, width, style, extend left/right, optional price and angle labels.

4. Horizontal line (full width, single click) and horizontal ray (starts at the clicked bar, extends right only, single click); both show a price label on the right edge and are draggable vertically, with colour/width/style settings.

Verification note: canvas rendering and drag interaction could not be exercised visually from this environment (no browser here) -- confirmed instead by PHP/JS lint and by tracing the R:R-lock and fib-level math by hand. Please run the ticket's own verification (place each tool; pan/zoom/switch timeframe/step and confirm anchoring holds; set 3:1, drag the stop, confirm TP follows; place an order from the tool and confirm it appears in the replay engine; refresh mid-session and confirm drawings return) after deploying.
